input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The join separator conditional was inverted during the move. The original code used "; " when any_prefix_is_slash was true and " / " otherwise. The new code uses "; " when it is false and " / " when it is true.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with both primary and secondary opts, such as a boolean flag like --shout/--no-shout. Mechanism: the swapped ternary picks the wrong separator. Impact: help output changes from "--shout / --no-shout" to "--shout; --no-shout", and slash-prefixed options (/debug; /no-debug) get " / " instead of "; ". This is a regression in every help screen with secondary opts.
critique: The finding identifies the same inverted conditional on any_prefix_is_slash. It describes the same swap of separators: "; " for normal options and " / " for slash-prefixed ones. It also gives the same examples, --shout/--no-shout and /debug.
